title: Watts, C. B. (1963). The Marginal Zone of the Moon. Astronomical Papers prepared for the use of the American Ephemeris and Nautical Almanac, Vol. XVII
note: The 1800 photographic limb charts at 0.2 deg steps in Watts angle, contour interval 0.2 arcsec. Not read in the original; its construction and datum are described from the VizieR VI/122 documentation, Morrison and Appleby 1981, Herald 1983 and Espenak's bulletins.

title: VizieR catalogue VI/122: The Marginal Zone of the Moon (Watts 1963), digitised by HMNAO and USNO, documentation file
note: Read in full. Gives the record layout of WATTS.TXT, the libration grid (L -9 to +9, B -8 to +8 in 0.2 deg steps), 1800 Watts-angle points per block, the +0.21 deg Watts-angle offset, the 1.564 versus 1.542 deg inclination correction, the accuracy codes, and the photograph sequences 1927 to 1956.

title: Morrison, L. V. and Appleby, G. M. (1981). Analysis of lunar occultations III. Systematic corrections to Watts' limb-profiles for the Moon. MNRAS 196, 1013-1020
note: Read in full from the ADS scan (OCR text). Source of the harmonic correction formula, the 1737.97 km datum radius, the +0.04 arcsec radius term, the -0.18 arcsec latitude shift, the -0.09 arcsec ellipticity, the +0.50 arcsec sin Q centre-of-figure term, and the 0.4 arcsec peak error.

title: Morrison, L. V. (1979). An analysis of lunar occultations in the years 1943-1974 for corrections to the constants in Brown's theory, the right ascension system of the FK4, and Watts' lunar-profile datum. MNRAS 187, 41
note: Paper I of the series. Not read; cited through Morrison and Appleby 1981 for the elliptical datum and the centre-of-figure displacement of 0.72 arcsec in longitude.

title: Herald, D. (1983). Correcting predictions of solar eclipse contact times for the effects of lunar limb irregularities. Journal of the British Astronomical Association 93, 241-246
note: Read in full from the ADS scan (page images). The displacement-curve method: h = 960 (M-1)(1-cos P), r = 0.97 M n arcsec per second, radial rate r cos(PA-N), the path-limit factor 1.863 km per arcsec times sqrt(sin^2 D / sin^2 a + cos^2 D), the limiting magnitudes for total and annular eclipses, and the error budget.

title: Fiala, A. D., Dunham, D. W. and Sofia, S. (1994). Variation of the solar diameter from solar eclipse observations, 1715-1991. Solar Physics 152, 97-104
note: Read pages 97-102 from the ADS scan. Describes the IOTA edge-observation method (Sofia, Dunham and Fiala 1979), its dependence on Watts data, and Table II of solar-radius corrections per eclipse relative to 959.63 arcsec.

title: Dunham, D. W., Sofia, S., Fiala, A. D., Herald, D. and Muller, P. M. (1980). Observations of a probable change in the solar radius between 1715 and 1979. Science 210, 1243-1245
note: Not read (paywalled); cited through Herald 1983 and Fiala et al. 1994 as the first published solar-radius result from eclipse-edge Baily's bead timings reduced with Watts profiles.

title: Espenak, F. and Anderson, J. (1999). Total Solar Eclipse of 2001 June 21. NASA/TP-1999-209484
note: Read from the local PDF text. Sections Mean Lunar Radius, Lunar Limb Profile and Limb Corrections to the Path Limits: Graze Zones. Source of the two k values, equations [8] and [9], the Lusaka worked example, Table 6 path corrections, the 5 to 10 km graze zone and the interior/exterior graze definitions.

title: Espenak, F. The Lunar Limb Profile and Eclipse Predictions. NASA Eclipse Web Site
note: Read. Summary of Watts, the 0.4 arcsec systematic errors, the 2 to 3 second uncorrected error, the 0.5 second Watts-corrected agreement and the 0.2 second Kaguya/LRO level.

title: Espenak, F. Lunar Limb Profile and Eclipse Predictions. EclipseWise
note: Read. Same text as the NASA page with the added statement that Kaguya and LRO data bring the accuracy to about 0.2 seconds.

title: Wright, E. and Young, C. A. (2024). A Raster-oriented Method for Creating Eclipse Maps. The Astronomical Journal 168, 163
note: Read through the IOP HTML in several targeted passes (the PDF download returned a script page). Source of the DEM-to-limb-profile algorithm, the L = 18000 bin recommendation, the 0.01 deg libration refresh threshold, the totality test rho, the 49-sided umbra, the 696000 km solar radius, DE440 and the Moon ME frame, and the Herald 1983 history.

note: Read (curl and pdftotext). Instructions for Occult 4 graze profiles: under Kaguya/LOLA profile data select LOLA with HiRes, leave Observed data at None because Watts-era observed corrections are obsolete; computing detailed profiles is computer-intensive.

title: Preston, S. (2019). Occult v4 Overview
note: Read from a local text copy. Confirms the LOLA lunar limb data download, the Show LOLA high resolution limb option on graze profiles, and the remark that with Gaia and LOLA grazes no longer yield unique limb information.

title: Dunham, D. W. (2026). Lunar Occultations. RASC Observer's Handbook 2026
note: Read (pdftotext). States that graze observations complement LRO laser ranging and have revealed small residual errors still under investigation, and that graze zones are 2 to 3 km wide.
